en: Udāna 5.10 Cūḷapanthakasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka was sitting not far from the Blessed One, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him.
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
whether standing, sitting, or lying down,"
A bhikkhu who is resolute in this mindfulness will obtain distinction between what precedes and what follows;
having obtained distinction between what precedes and what follows, he will attain the supreme state.
"May I go beyond the sight of the King of Death.
Tenth. The fifth chapter, the Soṇa-vagga, is concluded.
